newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco deliveries fall slightly in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Inco deliveries fall slightly in 1996.

text.p: Inco Ltd said on Tuesday that its deliveries of nickel fell slightly in 1996, but its own production rose slightly.

Total deliveries dropped to 558 million pounds of nickel in 1996, from 595 million pounds in 1995. But the company's own production rose to 412 million pounds in 1996 from 402 million in 1995. The company's finished inventories were 66 million pounds at the end of the year, compared to 57 million pounds at the end of 1995.
Inco was able to realize an average nickel price of US$3.35 per pound in the fourth quarter of 1996.
For the year, Inco said its average realized nickel price was US$3.61 per pound. In 1995, Inco's nickel prices averaged US$3.90 for the fourth quarter and US$3.86 per pound for the year.

As for copper, Inco's realized copper price averaged US$1.05 per pound in the fourth quarter and US$1.12 for the year, compared with 1995 average prices of US$1.22 per pound for the fourth quarter and US$1.29 per pound for the year.
Inco said it expects to report an after-tax gain of US$30 million in the first quarter of 1997, from the sale of Doncasters Plc, Inco's engineered products business.
Inco also said it plans to set aside US$27 million for more exploration at its huge nickel, copper and cobalt deposits at Voisey's Bay, Labrador.

The nickel company reported a large drop in earnings in the fourth quarter of 1996. Net profits for the quarter were US$26 million or US$0.09 a share compared to US$60 million or US$45 per share in 1995. For the year, net profits slid to US$179 million or US$1.09 a share from US$227 million or US$1.82 a share in 1995.
The company blamed lower metal prices for its lower earnings. ((Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8100))
